newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African police probe Pretoria city centre blazes.
newsitem.headline: S.African police probe Pretoria city centre blazes.

text.p: South African police were investigating an overnight blaze that extensively damaged the building housing offices of the "truth commission" into apartheid-era human rights abuses, a spokesman said on Tuesday.
The fire in Pretoria's main municipal building caused extensive damage to the eight-storey block.
The cause of the blaze was not yet known, said police spokesman Captain Morne van Wyk: "We are investigating a case of arson...That is routine in such a case."
Several fire fighters were treated for smoke inhalation, but no other injuries were reported.
Police believed arsonists were responsible for another fire on Monday night in a bank building a few blocks away. Van Wyk said police experts were investigating both blazes.
The municipal offices were still smouldering on Tuesday morning and council officials asked their 4,000 staff to stay at home for the day, state radio reported.
Truth commission officials, who had been using the municipal building to hear testimony on apartheid-era human rights abuses, were expected to postpone further hearings.
